shared_elements: carved stone surface in low relief
circular disc motif (a raised roundel in A; rosette discs in B)
horizontal banding/register lines near the lower part
justification: Both are stone reliefs that use a raised circular disc as a motif and organise some content into horizontal bands, but that is about as far as the correspondence goes. A is a heavily eroded three-dimensional block or statue whose ornament is barely legible and read frontally as a single mass, whereas B is a crisp, shallow, linear frieze of processing figures and animals in strict profile above a regular rosette border — utterly different in legibility, technique and compositional logic.
